title: Deploy CoachConnect to Railway
description: Deploy backend/ and frontend/ as two Railway services from the GitHub repo. Needs: persistent volume on backend for SQLite db + WhatsApp session, env vars set in Railway dashboard, nginx.conf made host/port-configurable (Railway private networking instead of docker-compose's automatic 'backend' DNS name).
close_reason: Both services live on Railway: backend (Express/Prisma/whatsapp-web.js) at backend-production-6b1d7.up.railway.app, frontend (React) at frontend-production-736a.up.railway.app. Persistent volume attached, env vars set, admin login confirmed working by Maroof. Fixed along the way: port must match the domain's target port on both services, railway.json needed to pin the Dockerfile builder (CLI inconsistently fell back to auto-detect), stale Chromium SingletonLock files block whatsapp-web.js after a container restart.

title: Get NIETE approval before expanding to all coaches
description: Present the working CoachConnect automation to NIETE management and get sign-off before Step 5 (opening the platform to other coaches). Required because it involves teacher data and organisational cost.

title: Isolate WhatsApp crashes from the rest of the backend
description: An uncaught exception from whatsapp-web.js/puppeteer (e.g. the 'onQRChangedEvent already exists' crash from a corrupted session) currently kills the entire Node process, taking down login/schools/templates/schedule along with it, not just the WhatsApp feature. Add a process-level safety net (e.g. isolate whatsappService.init() failures, or run Chromium in a way that a crash there can't bring down the Express server) so a WhatsApp-side problem degrades gracefully instead of taking the whole app offline.
